 3 O.S. No.2408/2007  JUDGMENT Suit is one for Permanent Injunction to restrain the defendant from interfering with the plaintiff's possession and enjoyment over the suit schedule property.

2. Case of the plaintiff's in brief is as hereunder:-
The plaintiff is the absolute owner in possession and enjoyment of the suit schedule property.

The schedule property was granted by the Government to his father Kunnappa as per the grant order dated 29.10.1955 and based on the grant order, the revenue entries are mutated in his name and plaintiff's father Sri. Kunnappa during his life time enjoyed the property as absolute owner thereof and he along with the plaintiff filed application to the Government seeking regularization of the grant of schedule property in his favour and accordingly, the Government has granted the schedule property to his use and occupation.

The defendant issued notification under Section 18(3) of the B.D.A. Act for acquisition of the schedule property and other portions of the Sy. No.17 of Doddakallasandra Village, Uttarahalli Hobli, Bengaluru South Taluk and final notification was also published by the B.D.A.

After coming to know of the said notifications, the plaintiff filed writ petition before the Hon'ble High Ramaiah vs The Commissioner Bda on 8 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/27357886/
2 Court of Karnataka in W.P. No.34567-569/1997 along with other persons.

sentences.text: The Hon'ble High Court passed a common order on 31.08.1998, wherein the writ petitions were allowed and the declarations issued by the B.D.A. were quashed by giving liberty to B.D.A. to pursue the acquisition from the stage of the representation filed by the plaintiff.
Immediately after the order, the plaintiff submitted representation/objection for acquisition of the land by the defendant.

The defendant after receiving the objection has not proceeded further and accordingly, no further declarations or award has been passed by the defendant and there was no taking of possession of the schedule property by the defendant.

Thus, the plaintiff continued to be in possession of the schedule property and the endorsement issued by the B.D.A. dated 14.03.2001 confirms that there were no further proceedings taken place in pursuance of the order of the Hon'ble High Court.

It is stated that the defendant through its contractors without there being any acquisition and there being any award or taking possession, in utter disobedience of the order of the Hon'ble High Court, made attempts to enter the suit property and the plaintiff and others got issued a common notice to the defendant on 05.01.2007.
Inspite of the service of notice, the defendant's officials and contractors made hectic efforts to form road in the layout and hence, left with no option, the present suit is filed.

3. In pursuance to the summons issued the defendant which is the B.D.A. caused appearance and filed written statement wherein which it is contended that the suit is liable to be dismissed for want of issuance of requisite statutory notice under Section 64 of B.D.A. Act.

It is contended that the property bearing Sy. No.17 totally measuring 25 acres 9 guntas situated at Doddakallasandra Village,
Uttarahalli Hobli, Bengaluru South Taluk was notified for acquisition by this defendant under preliminary notification dated 17.11.1988 and was published in the Karnataka Official Gazette dated 05.01.1989.
Pursuant to that a final notification was issued on 22.07.1991 in respect of Sy. No.17.

The Hon'ble High Court vide its order dated 31.08.1998 and 02.09.1998 in the writ petitions No.34567 to 34569/1997 connected with other writ petitions quashed the declaration by reserving liberty to the respondents i.e. the defendant herein to pursue the acquisition of lands after considering the objections.
In pursuance of the above order the B.D.A. authority in its meeting on 26.04.1999 vide B.R. No.54/1999 has over ruled the objection and resolved to move the Government to issue fresh notification.
Accordingly, the Government has issued final notification on 07.10.1999 published in Karnataka Gazette dated 07.10.1999.

After issuance of the final notification an award was passed on 07.08.2006 by Special Land Acquisition Officer to an extent of 23 acres 29 guntas and the same was approved by the Deputy Commissioner, Land Acquisition on 07.08.2006.
Pursuant to the award, the possession of 23 acres 29 guntas is taken under possession Mahazar dated 19.08.2006 and was handed over to the engineering wing on 19.08.2006 for the formation of layout.

The fact of taking possession on 19.08.2006 was notified under Section 16(2) of the B.D.A.
Act and the same was published in the Karnataka Gazette dated 18.01.2007 for public information.

The B.D.A. Employees Welfare Association had requested the Government and this defendant to allot lands for the purpose of formation of layout and considering their request, the Government,
under order dated 19.04.2006 accorded approval for allotment of lands.

Accordingly, an extent of 33 acres 2 guntas out of which an extent of 8 acres 26 guntas in Sy. No.15, an extent of 5 acres 22 guntas in Sy. No.16 and an extent of 18 acres 34 guntas in Sy. No.17 of Doddakallasandra Village was Ramaiah vs The Commissioner Bda on 8 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/27357886/
3 allotted to the B.D.A. Employees Welfare Association and the sale deed has been executed in favour of the society on 09.11.2006 and the possession is delivered to the society.

It is denied that the plaintiff is the absolute owner in possession and enjoyment of the suit schedule property and it is stated that the plaintiff has no right, title or interest over the suit schedule property and their claim as grantees is false.

It is stated that as per the order passed by the Hon'ble High Court, the acquisition proceedings are commenced after considering the objection of owners and the authority has over ruled the objections and issued fresh final notification on 07.10.1999 and hence, the plaintiff's claim that no decision has been taken by the defendant is untenable.
This defendant has considered the representations and thereafter, has issued final notification.

It is stated that the endorsement dated 14.03.2001 clearly shows Sy. Nos.15, 16 and 17 of Doddakallasandra Village have been notified and it is issued to the persons named therein and confined only to the extent of land for which the award has not been made and the said endorsement does not enure to the benefit of the plaintiff and other claimants.

It is contended that the defendant has formed layout in the suit schedule property and the plaintiff is not at all in possession and enjoyment of the same and hence,
the suit is not maintainable and is liable to be dismissed.

4. The aforesaid pleadings have occasioned following:-
ISSUES 1.
Whether plaintiff proves that he is in lawful possession over the suit schedule property as on the date of suit ?
2. Whether the plaintiff proves the alleged interference by the defendant in the suit schedule property ?
3. Whether the defendant proves that suit schedule property stood vested with it by virtue of acquisition ?
4. Whether the plaintiff is entitled for the relief of Permanent Injunction against defendant as prayed in the plaint ?
5. Whether suit is bad for want of notice under Section 64 of B.D.A. Act ?
6. What decree or order ?
5. The General Power of Attorney holder of plaintiff is examined as P.W.1 and he has relied upon 20 documents marked at Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.20 and closed the evidence.
On the contrary the defendant has not chosen to adduce evidence.

6. Heard learned counsel for the plaintiff and perused records.
7.
My answers to the above issues are as follows:

 REASONS 8. ISSUES NO.1 TO 4 :: All these issues are taken up collectively for common discussion to avoid repetition of facts and also for convenience of the Court.
The present suit is one for Permanent Injunction against the B.D.A.

The suit schedule property involved in the present suit is 01 acre 20 guntas of dry land in Sy. No.17 of Doddakallasandra Village, Uttarahalli Hobli, Bengaluru South Taluk which is bounded on East by - Kempanna's land,
West by - Road, North by - Kariyappa's land and South by - Sarkari Gomala.
9.
Before dealing with the controversy involved in the present suit, it is considered worth to take note of the undisputed facts of the case which is apparent from the record.
The suit schedule property bearing Sy. No.17 originally measured 25 acres 9 guntas situated at Doddakallasandra Village, Uttarahalli Hobli, Bengaluru South Taluk and the B.D.A.
by issuing preliminary notification dated 17.11.1988 has notified the said land for acquisition and it was published in Karnataka Gazette dated 05.01.1989.

Pursuant to that a final notification was issued on 22.07.1991 in respect of Sy.
No.17.

It is also apparent from the records that the plaintiff herein along with other persons challenged the notification before the Hon'ble High Court in Writ Petitions No.34567 to 34569/1997 and the Hon'ble High Court vide order dated 31.08.1998 has passed common order in all the writ petitions and the writ petition filed by the plaintiff herein is allowed and the relevant portion of the order passed by the Hon'ble is extracted as hereunder:
The rest of the petitions are allowed.

The declarations dated September 16, 1997,
September 17, 1997, September 17, 1997 and October 6, 1997 published in the Karnataka Gazette dated September 17, 1997, September 18, 1997, September 18,
1997 and October 6, 1997 respectively, issued under Section 19(1) of the Act are hereby quashed only in so far as they relate to the petitioners' land, leaving liberty to the respondents to issue fresh declaration if they are so advised only after considering the representations of the petitioners in accordance with Sec.18(1) of the Act.
It is made clear that in view of the sanction having been granted by the Government in accordance with Section 18(3) of the Act.

On the contrary, it is contention raised by the B.D.A. that pursuant to the order passed by the Hon'ble High Court, the authority has proceeded further and has called for the objections and vide its meeting dated 26.04.1999 vide B.R. No.54/1999 has over ruled the objections and proceeded to issue fresh notification and accordingly, final notification was issued on 07.10.1999 and award is passed on 07.08.2006 to an extent of 23 acres 29 guntas and possession is taken on 19.08.2006 and was handed over to the engineering wing on 19.08.2006 and sale deed has been executed in favour of society on 09.11.2006 pertaining to Sy. Nos.15, 16 and an extent of 18 acres 34 guntas in Sy.
No.17.

So according to this defendant, the defendant has not kept silent and it proceeded further and as per the direction of the Hon'ble High Court having considered the objection, has over ruled it and has acquired the suit schedule property and thus, the plaintiff is not in possession.
12.

So the burden is on the plaintiff to establish that, pursuant to the order of the Hon'ble High Court, he plaintiff has submitted objection for acquisition of the land and the defendant has considered the objection and has not proceeded further and no declarations or award has been passed and possession is not taken over and that the plaintiff continued to be in possession of the suit property.

The plaintiff in order to discharge the burden cast upon him got examined himself as P.W.1 and has in his affidavit deposed that, the schedule property was granted by the Government to his father Kunnappa as per the grant order dated 29.10.1955 and based on the grant order, the revenue entries are mutated in his name and plaintiff's father Sri. Kunnappa during his life time enjoyed the property as absolute owner thereof and he along with the plaintiff filed application to the Government seeking regularization of the grant of schedule property in his favour and accordingly, the Government has granted the schedule property to his use and occupation.

The defendant issued notification under Section 18(3) of the B.D.A. Act for acquisition of the schedule property and other portions of the Sy. No.17 of Doddakallasandra Village, Uttarahalli Hobli,
Bengaluru South Taluk and final notification was also published by the B.D.A.
After coming to know of the said notifications, the plaintiff filed writ petition before the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka in W.P. No.34567-569/1997 along with other persons.

The Hon'ble High Court passed a common order on 31.08.1998, wherein the writ petitions were allowed and the declarations issued by the B.D.A. were quashed by giving liberty to B.D.A. to pursue the acquisition from the stage of the representation filed by the plaintiff.
Immediately after the order, the plaintiff submitted representation/objection for acquisition of the land by the defendant.

The defendant after receiving the objection has not proceeded further and accordingly, no further declarations or award has been passed by the defendant and there was no taking of possession of the schedule property by the defendant.

Thus, the plaintiff continued to be in possession of the schedule property and the endorsement issued by the B.D.A. dated 14.03.2001 confirms that there were no further proceedings taken place in pursuance of the order of the Hon'ble High Court.

It is stated that the defendant through its contractors without there being any acquisition and there being any award or taking possession, in utter disobedience of the order of the Hon'ble High Court, made attempts to enter the suit property and the plaintiff and others got issued a common notice to the defendant on 05.01.2007.
Inspite of the service of notice, the defendant's officials and contractors made hectic efforts to form road in the layout and hence, left with no option, the present suit is filed.
13. In support of his evidence, he has relied upon Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.20.
Ex . P.1 is the G.P.A. executed by the plaintiff in favour of P.W.1 to prosecute the suit.

Ex.P.2 is the copy of the register of Darkhasth Ramaiah vs The Commissioner Bda on 8 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/27357886/
6 which shows the name of the plaintiff in the applicant column seeking grant of land in Sy. No.17 and the extent is not legible in the document.

sentences.text: Ex.P.3 is the endorsement issued by the B.D.A. dated 14.03.2001 and this is the document relying on which the plaintiff claims that the suit schedule property is not acquired by the B.D.A. and no further proceedings are initiated pursuant to the order of the Hon'ble High Court.

The endorsement issued by the B.D.A. shows that one Sri. Narayanappa along with 12 persons has submitted requisition on 24.01.2001 in respect of Sy. Nos.15, 16 and 17 wherein which they have submitted that they have no objection to acquire the land only for purpose of formation of road in the layout and to restore the remaining extent in Sy. Nos.15, 16 and 17 to its owners.

The said endorsement shows the lands available in Sy. Nos.15, 16 and 17 were acquired by issuing notification for the purpose of formation of J.P.Nagar, 9th Phase extension and since the 13 persons had submitted representations stating that the land required for formation of the road may be taken without compensation and sought to restore the remaining land, the said requisition was accepted and a portion of the land required for formation of road was taken over without compensation to the applicants and the remaining extent of the land is restored to them and it is left without acquisition.
But it is important to take note of the fact that, this document nowhere shows the name of the plaintiff and it is not clear as to whether the suit property was restored to the plaintiff.

Ex.P.4 is the letter dated 23.02.1998 issued to the Tahasildar by the Asst. Commissioner wherein which direction is issued to stop the formation of layout in Sy. Nos.16 and 17 and to supervise as to whether the B.D.A. has under taken any work in the said property.
Ex . P.5 to Ex.

P.9 are the Mahazar dated 31.08.1998 which shows the mahazar was conducted pertaining to Sy.
Nos.15, 16 and 17 in the presence of Sri. Narayanappa and others and this mahazar is conducted in order to ascertain as to whether the B.D.A. has under taken any formation of the layout in the property bearing Sy. No.15, 16 and 17 and it shows that no work has been under taken for formation of layout.
Ex . P.10
is the proceedings of the B.D.A. dated 01.07.1999.

Ex.P.11 is the notice dated 14.10.1998 issued by the B.D.A. to the plaintiff herein calling upon him to submit his objection pertaining to acquisition of 1 acre of land in Sy. No.17 within 3 dates from the date of receipt of notice failing which the B.D.A. will consider that there is no objection and the possession will be taken over by the authority.
Ex . P.12
and Ex

shows the suit schedule property stands in the name of plaintiff since the year 1990-91 to 1995-96 and mutation is accepted to his name based on the grant order passed by the Government and based on the Saguvali chit issued in favour of plaintiff.
Ex . P.14
is the tax paid receipt dated 13.01.1997 which shows tax is collected from the plaintiff.
Ex . P.15
is the document pertaining to Sy. No.15.
Ex . P.16 and Ex.P.17 are the notifications issued by the B.D.A. which are quashed by the Hon'ble High Court vide order dated 31.08.1998.

Ex . P.19 and Ex.P.20 are the letters dated 31.05.1999 issued by the Special Land Acquisition Officer to the Tahasildar calling upon the details as to the grant of land and as to the details of the grantees and the extent of the land granted pertaining to Sy. Nos.15, 16 and 17 and as per Ex.P.20.
14.

At this point of time, it is necessary to note that the defendant B.D.A. though caused appearance and raised several defenses in written statement, it has neither chosen to cross-examine P.W.1 nor has adduced any evidence on its behalf.
So there is absolutely no contradictory oral and documentary evidence available on record.

15. On analysis of the evidence of P.W.1 and the documents relied by him, Ex.P.2, Ex.P.12 and Ex.P.13 which are the Darkaast register extract and RTC and mutation extracts shows 1 acre of land Ramaiah vs The Commissioner Bda on 8 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/27357886/
7 in Sy. No.17 of Doddakallasandra Village is granted in favour of plaintiff vide order of the Deputy Commissioner dated 29.10.1955 and mutation is accepted as per M.R.No.59/92-93 and upto the year 1996 RTC stands in the name of the plaintiff.
The tax paid receipt shows he has paid tax in the year 1997.
Subsequent to that there are no revenue entries to show that suit schedule property has retain its agricultural character and the name of the plaintiff has continued in the revenue records.

So the revenue records are upto the year 1996-97 and there are no documents to show as on the date of filing of the suit, the RTC stands in the name of plaintiff pertaining to the said agricultural land of 1 acre 20 guntas and he is paying tax to the authority.

16. Now the contention of the plaintiff is that subsequent to the order of the Hon'ble High Court, the plaintiff submitted his objection to the defendant authority and the defendant authority has not proceeded for acquisition of the land and no declarations or award is passed and the possession is not taken over and there were no further proceedings initiated pursuant to the order passed by the Hon'ble High Court and he has solely relied upon the endorsement issued by the B.D.A. dated 14.03.2001.

Ex.P.3 is the said endorsement which is discussed herein before and it is issued on 14.03.2001 which shows that one Sri. Narayanappa and 12 others submitted representation pertaining to Sy. Nos.15, 16 and 17 and it is stated that some portion of the land in the said properties will be acquired without compensation for formation of the road and the remaining land will be restored to the applicants therein and the acquisition proceedings pertaining to the remaining portion of lands in Sy. Nos.15, 16 and 17 will be dropped.
But this document nowhere shows that the plaintiff is also one of the applicants.

So the said endorsement is only confined to a portion of land in Sy. No.15, 16 and 17 and only in respect of the applicants therein and in the absence of any document to show the plaintiff was one of the applicants and the suit property was also involved in the said representation, the endorsement does not enure to the benefit of the plaintiff and it is only confined to the persons who gave such representations.
Hence, Ex.P.3 is also of no assistance to plaintiff to show his possession over the suit property.

17. Now so far as, the other documents relied upon by the plaintiff i.e. Ex.P.4 to Ex.P.9 which are the letter communication between the revenue authorities and the mahazar conducted shows and it was conducted on 31.08.1998 i.e. the date on which the order was passed by the Hon'ble High Court.

So as on the said date the B.D.A. has not initiated any action for formation of layout and it can be presumed that owing to the pendency of the writ petition before the Hon'ble High Court the B.D.A.
has not initiated any proceedings.
So these documents also do not come to the aid of the plaintiff to establish his possession and that B.D.A has not proceeded further.
18. So now it is necessary to note that the defendant has left the suit uncontested.

But it has raised serious defense that that the as per the order of Hon'ble High Court, the defendant pursued the acquisition of lands after considering the objections and in its meeting on 26.04.1999 vide B.R.
No.54/1999 has over ruled the objection and the Government has issued final notification on 07.10.1999 and an award was passed on 07.08.2006 by Special Land Acquisition Officer to an extent of 23 acres 29 guntas and Pursuant to the award, the possession of 23 acres 29 guntas is taken under possession Mahazar dated 19.08.2006 and was handed over to the engineering wing on 19.08.2006 for the formation of layout and land was allotted to the B.D.A. Employees Welfare Association and the sale deed has been executed in favour of the society on 09.11.2006 and the possession is Ramaiah vs The Commissioner Bda on 8 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/27357886/
8 delivered to the society.

So when the B.D.A. has raised such a defense and when the written statement clearly shows the dates on which the notifications were issued, possession were taken and award was passed and 18 acres 34 guntas of land in Sy. No.17 along with other lands were sold in favour of society, the burden was on the plaintiff to establish that none of these proceedings were under taken.
So the defense raised by the defendant raises serious doubt as to the possession of the plaintiff over the suit property.

Added to this, Ex.P.11 relied upon by the plaintiff itself speaks that B.D.A. has issued notice on 14.10.1998 to the plaintiff calling upon him to submit his objection and this shows pursuant to the order of the Hon'ble High Court, the said notice is issued.

So this document speaks contrary to the contention raised by the plaintiff, that the B.D.A. has not initiated any action pursuant to the order passed by the Hon'ble High Court and this document nullifies the said contention raised by the plaintiff.

19. So under such circumstances, when the B.D.A. has initiated action for acquisition by issuing notice and when it has raised defense as to the acquisition of the suit property as discussed supra,
the burden was on the plaintiff to establish that no such notification was issued and no acquisition proceedings were completed.
But the plaintiff has not adduced convincing documents on record to disprove the said contention.

Further the plaintiff has also not produced revenue entries to show that the suit property has retained its agricultural character and the revenue records still stands in the name of the plaintiff as on the date of filing of the suit.
So if at all the acquisition proceedings were not completed, the revenue entries would have continued in the name of the plaintiff.
So all this circumstances creates doubts as to the possession of plaintiff over the suit schedule property.
Hence, the contention putforth by the plaintiff that no action is initiated by the defendant and he has continued to be in possession of the suit property is not proved.

Further it is also equally important to take note of the fact that, Sy. No.17 totally measures 25 acres 9 guntas and out of the total extent as per the notification dated 07.10.1999, 23 acres 29 guntas of the land is notified and the said extent of land is acquired and out of the total extent, 18 acres 34 guntas is sold in favour of the society.
So under such circumstances, the burden was on the plaintiff to establish that the suit schedule property was not part and parcel of the acquired land or the land sold in favour of society.

The plaintiff has absolutely not produced any piece of document to establish that the suit schedule property was not notified and it was dropped out of acquisition proceedings and that the B.D.A. has not initiated any action for acquisition of the suit property.
Hence, Ex.P.3 which is the endorsement do not enure to the benefit of the plaintiff, to establish that the suit property was not acquired.
So none of the documents produced by the plaintiff establishes his possession over the suit property as on the date of suit.

When the burden is on the plaintiff to establish his possession and when he has failed to discharge the same, just because the defendant has failed to adduce oral and documentary evidence, the plaintiff cannot be held entitled to the relief of Permanent Injunction as claimed.
Thus in view of the reasons assigned so far, this Court is of opinion that the plaintiff has failed to establish his possession and enjoyment over the suit property.

Though the defendant has failed to prove that the suit property vested with the B.D.A, by virtue of acquisition, since the plaintiff has failed to discharge the burden of proving his possession over the suit property, the plaintiff is not entitled for the relief claimed.
Accordingly, this Court proceeds to answer the aforesaid issues No.1 to 4 in the Negative.

ISSUE NO.5 ::
The present suit is filed by the plaintiff as against the B.D.A. seeking relief of Permanent Injunction.
The defendant has raised a specific defense that in view of non-compliance of issuance of statutory notice under Section 64 of B.D.A. Act, the suit is not maintainable.

Section 64 of the B.D.A. Act,1976, makes it clear that, no suit or proceedings shall be initiated against the authority without giving the authority one month's previous notice in writing of the intended suit or proceedings.
It is seen from the records that the plaintiff has not issued any notice to the defendant before the filing of the suit as required under the Act.
Further no application is filed along with the suit seeking dispensation of issuance of statutory notice to the defendant.
So since the plaintiff has not complied with the provisions of 64 of the B.D.A. Act, even on this count the suit is not maintainable.
Hence, this Court proceeds to answer the said issue No.5 is the Affirmative.

21. ISSUE NO.6 :: In view of findings on issues No.1 to 5, this Court proceeds to pass the following;
ORDER Suit of the plaintiff is dismissed.
Plaintiff shall bear the cost of the suit.
Draw decree accordingly.

 3 O.S. No.2408/2007  JUDGMENT Suit is one for Permanent Injunction to restrain the defendant from interfering with the plaintiff's possession and enjoyment over the suit schedule property.
opennyai_summary.facts:
The schedule property was granted by the Government to his father Kunnappa as per the grant order dated 29.10.1955 and based on the grant order, the revenue entries are mutated in his name and plaintiff's father Sri. Kunnappa during his life time enjoyed the property as absolute owner thereof and he along with the plaintiff filed application to the Government seeking regularization of the grant of schedule property in his favour and accordingly, the Government has granted the schedule property to his use and occupation.
The defendant issued notification under Section 18(3) of the B.D.A. Act for acquisition of the schedule property and other portions of the Sy. No.17 of Doddakallasandra Village, Uttarahalli Hobli, Bengaluru South Taluk and final notification was also published by the B.D.A.
The Hon'ble High Court passed a common order on 31.08.1998, wherein the writ petitions were allowed and the declarations issued by the B.D.A. were quashed by giving liberty to B.D.A. to pursue the acquisition from the stage of the representation filed by the plaintiff.
Immediately after the order, the plaintiff submitted representation/objection for acquisition of the land by the defendant.
The defendant after receiving the objection has not proceeded further and accordingly, no further declarations or award has been passed by the defendant and there was no taking of possession of the schedule property by the defendant.
Thus, the plaintiff continued to be in possession of the schedule property and the endorsement issued by the B.D.A. dated 14.03.2001 confirms that there were no further proceedings taken place in pursuance of the order of the Hon'ble High Court.
The Hon'ble High Court vide its order dated 31.08.1998 and 02.09.1998 in the writ petitions No.34567 to 34569/1997 connected with other writ petitions quashed the declaration by reserving liberty to the respondents i.e. the defendant herein to pursue the acquisition of lands after considering the objections.
In pursuance of the above order the B.D.A. authority in its meeting on 26.04.1999 vide B.R. No.54/1999 has over ruled the objection and resolved to move the Government to issue fresh notification.
Accordingly, the Government has issued final notification on 07.10.1999 published in Karnataka Gazette dated 07.10.1999.
After issuance of the final notification an award was passed on 07.08.2006 by Special Land Acquisition Officer to an extent of 23 acres 29 guntas and the same was approved by the Deputy Commissioner, Land Acquisition on 07.08.2006.

opennyai_summary.issue:
Whether plaintiff proves that he is in lawful possession over the suit schedule property as on the date of suit ?
2. Whether the plaintiff proves the alleged interference by the defendant in the suit schedule property ?
3. Whether the defendant proves that suit schedule property stood vested with it by virtue of acquisition ?
4. Whether the plaintiff is entitled for the relief of Permanent Injunction against defendant as prayed in the plaint ?
5. Whether suit is bad for want of notice under Section 64 of B.D.A. Act ?
6. What decree or order ?
[
10. Now the controversy involved in the present suit is that, according to the plaintiff after the order of the Hon'ble High Court, the plaintiff has submitted the objection for acquisition of the land by the defendant and the defendant after receiving the objection statement, has not proceeded further and no declarations or award has been passed and possession is not taken over and thus, the plaintiff continued to be in possession of the suit property and since there was interference by the defendant the present suit is filed.
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
The declarations dated September 16, 1997,
September 17, 1997, September 17, 1997 and October 6, 1997 published in the Karnataka Gazette dated September 17, 1997, September 18, 1997, September 18,
1997 and October 6, 1997 respectively, issued under Section 19(1) of the Act are hereby quashed only in so far as they relate to the petitioners' land, leaving liberty to the respondents to issue fresh declaration if they are so advised only after considering the representations of the petitioners in accordance with Sec.18(1) of the Act.
But it has raised serious defense that that the as per the order of Hon'ble High Court, the defendant pursued the acquisition of lands after considering the objections and in its meeting on 26.04.1999 vide B.R.
No.54/1999 has over ruled the objection and the Government has issued final notification on 07.10.1999 and an award was passed on 07.08.2006 by Special Land Acquisition Officer to an extent of 23 acres 29 guntas and Pursuant to the award, the possession of 23 acres 29 guntas is taken under possession Mahazar dated 19.08.2006 and was handed over to the engineering wing on 19.08.2006 for the formation of layout and land was allotted to the B.D.A. Employees Welfare Association and the sale deed has been executed in favour of the society on 09.11.2006 and the possession is Ramaiah vs The Commissioner Bda on 8 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/27357886/
8 delivered to the society.
So when the B.D.A. has raised such a defense and when the written statement clearly shows the dates on which the notifications were issued, possession were taken and award was passed and 18 acres 34 guntas of land in Sy. No.17 along with other lands were sold in favour of society, the burden was on the plaintiff to establish that none of these proceedings were under taken.
19. So under such circumstances, when the B.D.A. has initiated action for acquisition by issuing notice and when it has raised defense as to the acquisition of the suit property as discussed supra,
the burden was on the plaintiff to establish that no such notification was issued and no acquisition proceedings were completed.
The plaintiff has absolutely not produced any piece of document to establish that the suit schedule property was not notified and it was dropped out of acquisition proceedings and that the B.D.A. has not initiated any action for acquisition of the suit property.
Hence, Ex.P.3 which is the endorsement do not enure to the benefit of the plaintiff, to establish that the suit property was not acquired.
So none of the documents produced by the plaintiff establishes his possession over the suit property as on the date of suit.
When the burden is on the plaintiff to establish his possession and when he has failed to discharge the same, just because the defendant has failed to adduce oral and documentary evidence, the plaintiff cannot be held entitled to the relief of Permanent Injunction as claimed.
Though the defendant has failed to prove that the suit property vested with the B.D.A, by virtue of acquisition, since the plaintiff has failed to discharge the burden of proving his possession over the suit property, the plaintiff is not entitled for the relief claimed.
